546 AM CDT Wed Apr 29 2026
If conditions become unrepresentative...contact the National Weather

.DISCUSSION...
Some patchy fog is possible but not likely thru early this 
morning. Winds will be generally light as a frontal boundary 
begins to push into the region this afternoon. Expect light 
southerly winds ahead of the front and light northerly winds 
behind the front. Winds will generally be light throughout the day
outside of any storms with occasional wind gusts around 10-15 
mph. Current best timing for the front is in the mid to late 
afternoon in northwestern Montgomery County. Additional rounds of 
showers and isolated storms are anticipated later today thru 
Friday along a stalled/meandering frontal boundary. A few storms 
could be strong to severe with locally heavy rainfall possible. 
Afternoon minimum RH should generally remain above 70 percent 
through Friday.

.DISCUSSION...
Gusty southerly winds expected today with sustained winds around 
10-15 mph with gusts around 25 mph in the afternoon hours. Minimum 
RH values this afternoon will be around 50 percent. Monitoring the
potential for isolated showers and thunderstorms during the 
overnight hours, but rain chances increase on Wednesday. A slow
moving frontal boundary begins to push into the Brazos Valley on 
Wednesday afternoon and scattered to widespread showers and storms
are expected to develop along the boundary. Winds ahead of the 
front on Wednesday morning will start out light and southerly and 
transition to westerly then northerly behind the front. Wind 
speeds are anticipated to remain below 10 mph on Wednesday outside
of any storms. Locally higher winds will be possible around any 
storms.

the morning, and diminishing to SW at 8-10 mph in the afternoon.

and lift to about 6-7 kft after 2 PM underneath upper level clouds.

transport winds will lead to ADI values just under 60 in the late 
afternoon.

tonight, RH values under 85 percent should inhibit fog development 
overnight into Tuesday morning at the burn site. Please feel free to 
contact us if you have any further questions or concerns.

.DISCUSSION...
A frontal system slowly approaching from the Great Lakes and 
Northeast will drop into the area tonight. Near record warm  
temperatures are expected ahead of the front. Even though dew 
points will also be rising, the large spread with the temperatures
will result in afternoon RH in the 30s and 40s. Winds will be west
to southwest but not quite as gusty as recent days, with a shift
to south possible for a time this evening east of the Blue Ridge
Mountains and south of US-50. Shifts to the north, east, then
southeast are anticipated tonight as the front drops south.
The front will stall nearby or overhead through Thursday, 
increasing the potential for showers and thunderstorms. There will
also be a large contrast in temperatures from northeast to 
southwest across the area on Thursday. Winds should be light but
with variable directions given the front nearby. RH will also be
notably higher given onshore flow.
The front will lift northward as a warm front Friday ahead of a 
strong cold front approaching from the west. The next opportunity
for more numerous showers and perhaps some thunderstorms will 
occur with this front on Sunday.

.DISCUSSION...A strong ridge has set up to our southeast,
encompassing much of Kentucky. Meanwhile, multiple disturbances are
expected to develop across the Plains and move northeastward through
the Ohio Valley, but will have a hard time making it into the 
Commonwealth due to that ridge. Instead, Kentucky will find itself 
in a strong SW flow pattern well into the first part of the weekend, 
and in the unstable sector on the south side of a frontal boundary. 
This will keep enough moisture in the region for min RH levels to 
stay generally in the 30-50% range each afternoon. Mixing will also 
produce some gusty conditions over the next few days during the 
daytime hours. Given our position in the warm, moist, and unstable 
sector of these systems, can't rule out some shower and thunderstorm 
chances each day, mainly during the afternoon when mixing/heating are
at their best. However, with the ongoing ridging aloft, the storms
are not expected to be widespread, organized, or severe. The ridge 
then begins breaking down by this weekend, with a potent cold front 
and better rain/storm chances moving across eastern Kentucky late 
Saturday into Sunday morning.
